description:
FILED s473f (Opus, 2026-09-09), as the measured residue of #1308.

    open(my $fh, ">", $F) or die;
    my $g = *$fh;
    ref(\$g)      perl: GLOB     PCL: REF   (was SCALAR before #1308)

For a TYPEGLOB the discriminator is the BOX's is-ref flag (#163's rule, see
%p-glob-value-box-p): `$g = *foo` is a glob VALUE (ref "" ), `$g = \*foo` is a
glob REF (ref "GLOB").  A FILEHANDLE payload carries no such flag -- `open` box-
sets the raw stream -- so #1308 had to choose one answer for both spellings and
chose GLOB, which is right for the COMMON shapes (`ref($fh)`, `my $b = $fh;
ref($b)`, `ref($a[0])` on an element handle) and wrong for this one.

Setting is-ref at %p-install-fh would need the flag to PROPAGATE on copy, which
for typeglobs is spelled out across box-set, %p-flatten-list,
%p-array-store-scalar, p-aref-unbox-elem, p-flatten-args and p-return-value --
a wide change for one exotic shape.  Measure the population before doing it.

Related: `"$$fh"` is `*main::$fh` in perl (the anonymous glob's NAME) and
GLOB(0x...) in PCL; PCL has no anonymous glob to name.
subject: PCL cannot tell a glob VALUE from a glob REF for a FILEHANDLE: `my $g = *$fh; ref(\$g)` is REF where perl says GLOB
